## Installation

Install the development version of `DAPS` from GitHub.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# install the package via devtools
install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("wnbo9/DAPS")
# load the package
library(DAPS)
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
library(DAPS)
```

## DAPS with Individual-level Data

### Example data

We use the `N3finemapping` data from `susieR`: genotypes of
`r nrow(susieR::N3finemapping$X)` individuals at
`r ncol(susieR::N3finemapping$X)` SNPs in one region, with a simulated
phenotype that has three causal SNPs.

```{r}
data(N3finemapping, package = "susieR")
X <- N3finemapping$X
y <- N3finemapping$Y[, 1]
n <- nrow(X)

true_causal <- which(N3finemapping$true_coef[, 1] != 0)
true_causal
```

### Running DAP-S

`daps()` takes the genotype matrix `X` and phenotype `y`. `L` is the
maximum number of causal effects allowed in the region.

```{r}
rst <- daps(X, y, L = 10)
names(rst)
```

The result is a list with the following elements:

| Element | Description |
|---|---|
| `pip` | Variant-level posterior inclusion probabilities |
| `prior` | Variant-level prior inclusion probabilities |
| `models` | Plausible model configurations and their posterior probabilities |
| `twas_weights` | TWAS weights (default is NULL) |
| `info` | Additional details: complete signal clusters, CPIP, per-signal PIPs, stored models and LD |
| `sets` | Desired signal clusters (default) or credible sets |
| `variants` | Variant-level table of SNPs in each signal cluster or credible set (fastENLOC-style) |

The `rst$pip` gives the posterior probability of each variant being causal.
```{r}
head(rst$pip)
data.frame(pip = rst$pip[true_causal], row.names = true_causal)
```

The `rst$models` lists the plausible model configurations evaluated by DAP-S, with
their log10 Bayes factor, log10 prior, log10 unnormalized posterior, and
posterior model probability:
```{r}
head(rst$models)
```


### Signal clusters and credible sets

By default (`coverage = NULL`), `DAPS` reports **signal clusters**. A signal cluster is a group of correlated SNPs that together represent a single association signal: the data show that one of them is likely causal, but cannot tell which. Each cluster contains SNPs whose pairwise absolute correlation is at least `min_abs_corr` (default 0.5).

```{r}
rst$sets
```

For signal clusters, `coverage` is the cluster PIP (CPIP): the posterior
probability that the cluster contains a causal SNP. For credible sets,
it is instead the summed within-signal PIP of the SNPs in the set. 
`daps_plot()` visualizes the results. The top panel shows the PIP of each
SNP, and the bottom panel shows the signal clusters (or credible sets)
with their coverage.

```{r, fig.alt = "DAPS PIP and signal cluster plot"}
daps_plot(rst)
```

Signal clusters enable the construction of credible sets at any level
$\rho$, using `get_set()` without refitting. For example, the 95%
credible sets ($\rho = 0.95$) are:

```{r, fig.alt = "DAPS PIP and 95% credible set plot"}
rst_cs <- rst
rst_cs$sets <- get_set(rst, coverage = 0.95)
rst_cs$sets
daps_plot(rst_cs)
```

## DAPS with Sufficient Statistics

`DAPS` can also run on **sufficient statistics**:
$\boldsymbol{X}^T\boldsymbol{X}$, $\boldsymbol{X}^T\boldsymbol{y}$,
$\boldsymbol{y}^T\boldsymbol{y}$ and $n$. This is useful
when individual-level data cannot be shared. Here we compute them from centered `X` and `y`.

```{r}
X_c <- scale(X, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)
y_c <- y - mean(y)
XtX <- crossprod(X_c)
Xty <- as.numeric(crossprod(X_c, y_c))
yty <- sum(y_c^2)

rst_ss <- daps_ss(XtX, Xty, yty, n, L = 10)
rst_ss$sets$sets
```


## DAPS with Summary Statistics

A common scenario in genetics is having only GWAS **summary statistics**.
`daps_rss()` takes z-scores `z` and an LD matrix `R`, along with the
sample size `n` if available. Alternatively, effect size estimates `bhat`
and their standard errors `shat` can be supplied instead of `z`.

```{r}
ss <- susieR::univariate_regression(X, y)
z <- ss$betahat / ss$sebetahat
R <- cor(X)

rst_rss <- daps_rss(z = z, R = R, n = n, L = 10)
rst_rss$sets$sets
```
